page: Amazon Web Services r6a.24xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by a 48-core, 96-thread AMD EPYC 7R13 processor operating at up to 3.6 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Memory configuration includes 768.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, providing a generous 1:8 core-to-memory ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware security extensions such as AES, VAES, SHA-NI, and IBRS are present, though AVX-512 and AMX extensions are absent. Networking bandwidth provides a 38 Gbps baseline. There is no bundled local NVMe storage and no dedicated GPU hardware attached to this configuration.

Benchmark results demonstrate high multi-threaded compute and in-memory processing capabilities. The instance achieved a top-tier stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 143,459.57 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 16,764.0, complemented by strong results in code compilation (53,862.0) and ray tracing (90,633.0). Memory throughput is robust for cached access, registering 6,045.09 GB/sec on small blocks, though uncached large-block throughput falls to an average 133.64 GB/sec read and 65.65 GB/sec write. In-memory operations perform well, highlighted by 92.53 million Redis SET operations per second and strong PassMark database operations.

From a cost-efficiency and operational standpoint, the r6a.24xlarge provides dense memory capacity per core on AMD hardware, serving as an economical option for enterprise workloads requiring large memory footprints without paying for local storage drives. However, reliance on network-attached storage requires factoring in EBS provisioning. It is well-suited for large in-memory databases, Redis caches, high-concurrency analytical queries, and large-scale data processing.
description: Amazon Web Services r6a.24xlarge is a memory-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, featuring a 48-core, 96-thread AMD EPYC 7R13 processor clocked at 3.6 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the instance pairs 96 vCPUs with 768.0 GB of DDR4 memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per vCPU allocation. Networking is provisioned with a 38 Gbps baseline, with no local storage or GPUs bundled. In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates top-tier multi-threaded compute with a stress-ng multi-core score of 143,459.57, top-tier cryptographic performance, and high-throughput memory caching supporting 92.53 million Redis SET operations per second. While single-thread and uncached memory operations fall in the middle tier, the high memory-to-vCPU ratio offers strong qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive setups. The r6a.24xlarge is particularly fitted for enterprise in-memory caches, distributed databases, real-time analytics, and data processing engines.
